bug_semantics: Traefik Kubernetes Gateway provider option crossProviderNamespaces is documented as allowing only listed Gateway API route namespaces to declare TraefikService backendRefs such as api@internal, dashboard@internal, or rest@internal. For HTTPRoute rules with a single internal backend, the provider correctly checks route.Namespace. For mixed/WRR rules, loadService overwrites namespace from backendRef.Namespace (legitimate for core Service lookup and ReferenceGrant) and then loadHTTPBackendRef runs isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed against that target namespace. An HTTPRoute in a non-allow-listed namespace can therefore add an @internal TraefikService to the generated WRR graph by setting backendRef.namespace to an allow-listed namespace that has issued a Gateway API ReferenceGrant, exposing the dashboard/API on the data plane without changing Traefik static config or RBAC.
flaw_origin: CrossProviderNamespaces was first implemented on the v2.11 line in 28604083a41b6d6e8c206d71e0bce464bff1edb7 (PR #13094), where loadServices was called with route.Namespace and WRR rejected @internal members outright, so that tree does not have this bypass. The first public write of the flawed mechanism is merge 8c7634bcde599dd14d4d5c1346acd734f3a007a1 (PR #13116, Merge branch v2.11 into v3.6): conflict resolution inserted the allowlist check into v3.6 httproute.go loadHTTPBackendRef, which already received the backendRef-overwritten namespace. Neither merge parent contains those httproute.go lines. The check then shipped in v3.6.17 and was merged to v3.7 in e116b8b8595b7917f4340ee2d916444f33d720e4 (first in v3.7.1).

reasoning: CVE-2026-54761 / GHSA-3g6v-2r68-prfc is a real, published (not withdrawn) authorization bypass of Kubernetes Gateway crossProviderNamespaces on HTTPRoute mixed/WRR backendRefs. The intended control is the route namespace; the WRR path instead authorized against backendRef.namespace after loadService overwrote it, so an untrusted HTTPRoute plus a ReferenceGrant from an allow-listed namespace could attach api@internal. The smallest first-write of those vulnerable httproute.go lines is merge 8c7634bcde599dd14d4d5c1346acd734f3a007a1: immediate first parent 801eb2f149fb0d50cfa706abb741a1c0ae4c7800 lacks the check, the v2.11 second parent implemented a correct route-namespace check in a different file, and no squash member reconstructs the v3.6 insertion. That merge precedes v3.6.17 / v3.7.1 and the fix 8447bfc71e971ed150d610d67ca261d64253695c lands at v3.6.21 / v3.7.5.
